name: Encyclopædia Britannica (11th ed., Vols. 1–29). (1910–1911). Cambridge University Press.
description: Twenty-nine-volume general English-language encyclopedia (40,000 entries), edited by Hugh Chisholm and published by Cambridge University Press; the first Britannica to be issued complete and in a single alphabetical sequence, and the first with a comprehensive categorical index (vol. 29). Assembled during the work's transition from a British to an American publication, it remains a public-domain record of pre-World-War-I scientific, historical, and scholarly knowledge, though much of its content is obsolete or reflects the prejudices of its era.

events.event: Cambridge University Press begins publication of the 29-volume eleventh edition
Publication completes with vol. 29, the index volume

metadata.sourceReference: 29 volumes, not 20: the 1911 edition is the eleventh (29 vols, 28 text + index), published 1910-1911 by Cambridge University Press under editor-in-chief Hugh Chisholm. Per-volume references use the uploader's split items encyclopedia-britannica-volume-1..29 (all 1911 / eng / no access restriction / public domain, PDF+EPUB+JP2 each), not the single container item encyclopedia-britannica-volume-14_202405 (which holds all 29 volumes in 324 files despite its 'volume-14' identifier). Verified by title-page OCR: vols 1 and 14 read 'THE ENCYCLOPAEDIA BRITANNICA ELEVENTH EDITION'; vol. 29 reads 'INDEX TO ... ELEVENTH EDITION', confirming it as the index volume. Letter ranges cross-checked against the Wikipedia volume table. No identifier recorded: the work predates ISBN assignment. Verified 2026-10-05.

description: A composite manuscript volume at the Real Biblioteca Digital (item 20771), catalogued under the title of its first component, a 1755 memoir on hemp by Dodart (intendant of Berry) with additions by Marcandier, conseiller à la cour de justice de Bourges. The components relevant here are: ff. 56v-57r, Real Orden from Julián de Arriaga to Joaquín de Maguna (Aranjuez, 31 May 1775); ff. 57r-60r, the Informe made pursuant to that order (Ferrol, 2 August 1775); ff. 60r-66v, the papers cited in that report; and ff. 66v-74v, the asiento (supply contract) awarded to Manuel Martín, agent for Phelipe Chone, to supply hemp for five years. Concerns, in the source's own terms: sectoral policy, technology, and industrial supply.

description: Single-sheet memorial (8 folios, in-quarto format) by the arbitrists Francisco Martínez de Mata, 'natural de Motril, siervo de los pobres afligidos', arguing for the remedy of Spain's depopulation and poverty. Imprint [S.l. : s.n., ca. 1626]; the 1626 date is taken from the verso of leaf 2, and the title from the opening words of the text. Digitised from the Fondo Antiguo of the Biblioteca de la Universidad de Sevilla (sign. A 110/127(67); collection PABI 2006-3). This original imprint complements the modern collected edition (Memoriales y discursos) held separately.

name: Martínez de Mata, F. (1650). Memoriales y discursos.
description: Composed c. 1650-1670; no seventeenth-century printing exists in digital form, so the linked Google Books record is the standard 1971 edition (Madrid, Moneda y Crédito, ed. Gonzalo Anes), which the source table lists simply as Memoriales. Google Books reports viewability "no pages" for this edition, so it is a catalogue record only and the text is not readable online. Concerns, in the source's own terms: industry, manufactures, labour, commerce, and economic decadence. description: First modern treatise of political economy published in Spain, in the classical tradition of Smith and Say: a theoretical synthesis followed by an application to the Spanish case. Licensed in January–February 1829 and dedicated to Fernando VII; an official university textbook for a generation, reaching three editions in eleven years. Library catalogues sometimes attribute the work to Eusebio María del Valle; economic-history scholarship assigns it to Francisco de Gregorio, marqués de Valle Santoro.
